To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phenolic Mannich base compounds 1–15 are weak inhibitors of the human carbonic anhydrases hCA I and II.

(1) Mannich bases with phenolic group were prepared starting from 1; (2) Mannich bases were evaluated on hCA I, hCA II, and (3) Mannich bases showed lower inhibition percentages on hCA I than on hCA II.
the phenolic Mannich base derivatives 2–15 are less potent than 1 as inhibitors of hCA I and II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structural characterization, and carbonic anhydrases (CAs) inhibitory activities of a series of Mannich bases containing the phenol functional unit.

the synthesis and biological evaluation of phenolic Mannch bases, which may be used in the treatment of glaucoma, as well as in the treatment of other diseases, in which CA inhibition plays an important role.
the synthesis of Mannich bases incorporating the phenol function, which is a structural motif found in several natural and synthetic CA inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the phenolic group is not enough for a good CA inhibitor, as the presence of the amine group is also necessary.

the phenolic Mannich base derivatives of 1,3,5-trisubstituted aromatic amines (compounds 2–7) were the most potent hCA I and II inhibitors, while the phenolic Mannic bases of 4-substituted aromatic amina (compounds 8–15) had the lowest inhibition percentages on the both isoforms.
the Mannich base derivatives 1–15 have low inhibitory effects on the hCA I and II isozymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a phenol group in a compound does not necessarily increase its inhibitory activity on hCA isoenzymes.
the phenolic Mannich base derivatives of 1 were not very effective CA inhibitors.

the presence of the Mannich base moiety in the structure of the compounds 2–15 did not increase the CA inhibitory power of the compounds, and the phenol moiety is the only functional group responsible for the inhibitory power of compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mannich bases 1–15 are weak CA inhibitors.
the Mannich bases 1–15, which were synthesized from 4-hydroxy benzyliden indenones, are not potent CA inhibitors.
the Mannich bases 1–15 are less potent inhibitors of the hCA I and II than the reference sulfonamides, but they have a similar selectivity profile as the reference sulfonamines.
